The gift, object and program routes each reprint the H1 'A public collection for internet-native art' and the same lede above their own title, so 'CENTURY #31' and 'Casey Reas donation from punk6529' are smaller headings below the generic museum headline.

The program status chip shows a raw enum in Title Case that joins two states: 'Selection Complete Acquisition And Accession Unverified'. The object page shows a record-type chip, 'Accession object record', next to 'Accessioned' (object-1440x1000-01.png). The gift chips use Title Case: 'Formally Accepted' (gift-1440x1000-01.png).

The gift subtitle is a generic methodology disclaimer, not a description of this gift: 'A transfer or custody reference is not, by itself, an accession. Each lot keeps its current gate visible.' Field labels are internal: 'CUSTODY REFERENCE' (networkmuseum.6529.eth) and 'RECEIPT EVIDENCE', whose value is a full 66-character transaction hash with the date. 'Completion limits' is a section heading followed only by '—'. On the object page, the back link 'Back to accession' does not say which accession, and 'Technical evidence' is internal wording (object-1440x1000-01.png).

Under 'CENTURY #31 / Casey REAS' there is no plain label line with date and medium. The first paragraph reads like a verification log: 'On-chain generative software associated with an ERC-721 token on Ethereum; Art Blocks records a token hash. Determinism of live behavior has not yet been independently verified.' The fine print reads: 'This token is one comparative state in a three-token CENTURY sample… it is not an artist-defined triptych.' The 'Artist statement' panel contains a third-person paraphrase ('The artist describes CENTURY as…') with no source.

On the program route, the eyebrow 'PROGRAMS' repeats the heading 'Programs', and the program itself, 'Keys and Gates', appears only as a card title under the internal code '6529NM-AP-01'. Its subtitle starts in lowercase: 'photographs of access, control, and exit'. The intro is abstract: 'Programs give the Museum a curatorial frame, a public process, and a documented route from selection to acquisition.'
